claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in high-entropy alloys is governed by wear-induced microstructural refinement.
Wear-induced microstructural refinement accelerates the formation and stabilization of a passivating oxide film.
The protective film generated during wear is enriched in corrosion-resistant elements such as Mo.
Dynamic regeneration of the passivation film mitigates material loss under combined mechanical and corrosive attack.
The proposed initial material is a homogenized, entropy-stabilized, single-phase CoCrFeNi-based HEA containing a moderate amount of Mo.
Adding Mo to the FeCoCrNi alloy system can improve wear resistance.
Adding Mo to the FeCoCrNi alloy system can improve passivation-film stability and corrosion resistance.
Sliding contact under combined wear-corrosion conditions produces dynamic nanocrystallization and a high dislocation density at the contact surface.
The refined, defect-rich surface has greater reactive area and faster oxide-formation kinetics.
Mo/Cr-rich oxides rapidly heal passivation-film damage caused by wear.
Rapid passivation-film healing synergistically reduces both effective wear and corrosive attack.
A high-Mo alloy will have lower wear-volume loss during combined tribocorrosion than a matched low-Mo alloy.
A high-Mo alloy will have lower corrosion-current density during combined tribocorrosion than a matched low-Mo alloy.
A high-Mo alloy will have a more stable passivation film during combined tribocorrosion than a matched low-Mo alloy.
The high-Mo versus low-Mo differences will be less pronounced in isolated wear and isolated corrosion tests than in the combined test.
The low-Mo baseline does not favor rapid or robust passivation-film formation under wear contact.
The proposed mechanism should operate under moderate mechanical loads in chloride-rich aqueous environments.
The mechanism should fail when mechanical or corrosive stress overwhelms film healing, including under extreme acid exposure.
Prior studies support improved wear resistance, corrosion resistance, and passivation-film stability with increased Mo.
The benefit under combined wear-corrosion will exceed the additive effects observed in separate wear and corrosion tests.
